key_insight: OperAItor combines LLM agents with process monitoring and action validation to reduce simulated chemical-plant shutdowns during faults.
engineering_relevance: The open-source framework offers a reproducible benchmark for supervisory fault management above conventional process controls and safety systems.
method: Integrate statistical monitoring, fault diagnosis, knowledge-graph retrieval, and action planning.
Compare five action-validation configurations, including no validation, an LLM judge, digital-twin simulation, and deterministic checks.
Test four LLMs on a 113-variable reactor–distillation model across 20 fault scenarios.
evidence_signal: Without intervention, 18 of 20 scenarios stopped the simulated plant; validated configurations using GPT-5 nano, Qwen3 8B, and Mistral 7B reduced stops to 5–8 and recovered $265,000 under benchmark economics.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; deployment requires validation against real plant dynamics, safety constraints, and operating economics.
paper_title: OperAItor: An Agentic Framework for Fault-Tolerant Operation of Chemical Processes
